chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted is more intensely joyful with the repentance of His servant than a man who lost his mount and his provisions during a dark night, and then found them. So, Allah is more intensely joyful with the repentance of His servant than that man was when he found his mount.'
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran and Hadith describe Allah's joy in repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the profound divine joy in repentance, using the simile of a traveler finding his lost mount in a dark night to illustrate Allah's delight surpassing human relief. In Shia scholarship, this narration is often cited to emphasize the accessibility of divine mercy and the importance of sincere tawbah, reinforcing the concept that Allah's forgiveness is not merely a legal absolution but an emotional and spiritual reunion. The comparison underscores the value of the servant's return to God, suggesting that the joy of forgiveness is a central attribute of the Divine.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted is more Intensely Happier with the repentance of His<sup>azwj</sup> servant than a man would be whose ride and his provision has strayed during a dark night, and he finds it. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more intensely Happy with the repentance of His<sup>azwj</sup> servant than that man would be when he finds his ride’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following: “

I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah, the Most High, is more pleased for the repentance of His servant than one who loses his animals, that carry his load and supplies, in a dark night and then finds them out. Allah is more pleased for the repentance of His servant than the person who finds his lost properties.’”
